newsitem.title: USA: Simpson civil trial jury sees grisly photo.
newsitem.headline: Simpson civil trial jury sees grisly photo.

text.p: Jurors in the O.J. Simpson civil trial were shown a grisly picture on Friday of Nicole Brown Simpson lying dead in a pool of blood and a witness described finding the former football player's ex-wife slashed to death.
Simpson, who was acquitted in October 1995 of murdering his ex-wife and her friend, Ronald Goldman, was not in court for the afternoon session when the photograph was shown on a big screen.
Jurors looked intently at the picture in which the upper portion of Nicole Brown Simpson's body could be seen on the walkway of her home with a trail of blood stretching down toward the sidewalk.

On the first day of testimony in the civil case, Sukru Boztepe, a neighbour of Nicole Brown Simpson, told how he was led to the murder scene by Nicole's agitated Akita dog that had been found wandering in the street.
When he looked up the walkway in the direction the dog was looking, he said: "I saw a lady lying down, full of blood."
"I could see just that she was blonde and I could see her arm. I told my wife there was a dead person there," Boztepe said, adding he went to the house of a neighbour who called the police.
Earlier, another witness testified he heard two men arguing outside Nicole Brown Simpson's home on the night she and Goldman were murdered.

Robert Heidstra, a neighbour, said he was walking his dogs and heard the argument at around 10:40 p.m., and about five minutes later saw a white Jeep-like vehicle similar to Simpson's speeding away from the scene.
He testified he was in an alleyway across from Nicole Brown Simpson's condominium when "I heard a clear voice saying 'hey, hey' hey' about three or four times. It was a clear young voice."
He then heard another older, deeper voice talking very fast. "It sounded like an argument." About 15 seconds later, Heidstra said he heard the gate to her property slam.

Simpson was acquitted in a criminal trial in October 1995 of murdering his ex-wife and Goldman. He is being sued in a wrongful death suit by the victims' families. If found liable, Simpson could be forced to pay millions of dollars in damages.

Attorney Daniel Petrocelli, who represents Goldman's father, told jurors in his opening statement on Wednesday that Simpson would have had plenty of time to commit the murders at 10:45 p.m. and get back to his home nearby in time to meet a limousine driver at 11 p.m. who was taking him to the airport for a flight to Chicago.

By using Heidstra to establish the time of the murders at around 10:45 p.m., the plaintiffs have pushed back the time-line from the one used by prosecutors in the criminal trial. They relied on other witnesses to establish the time of the murders at about 10:30 p.m.
The significance of establishing a different time-line was not clear.
Heidstra said that before the apparent argument, he heard the Akita dog "barking like crazy, confused, panicky. I thought My God, what's going on here?"

Shown a picture of Simpson's white Ford Bronco, Heidstra, a car detailer, said, "I can't say exactly it was this car, but it resembles the size of this car." Heidstra said the vehicle "must have been in a hurry. It sped away fast.'

In other testimony on Friday, a waiter who worked with Goldman rejected the defence contention that Goldman and Nicole Brown Simpson were dating. "He (Goldman) didn't say he had a date with Nicole," Stewart Tanner testified.

Simpson's lawyers argued on Thursday that the ex-football star and movie actor had been upset that his ex-wife had been partying with prostitutes and drug dealers and that she had become pregnant by a boyfriend and had an abortion.
